narrative.overview:
A light working tool, not a dashboard. The page is a pale cool ground (`ground`) tinted by three large blurred colour washes (blue top-left, lilac right, peach bottom), with an extra lilac pool behind the result column. On that ground sit solid white input cards that behave like paper: opaque, softly shadowed, never translucent. Glass appears only on surfaces that stay put while content scrolls beneath them: the sticky header pill, the sticky result panel, and the mobile dock. The single gradient (blue to violet to rose) belongs to the result card, which is the one loud object on the page.

Density is moderate and form-led: labelled fields, segmented controls, and tables of figures. Every number is set in tabular figures because users compare these amounts against payment receipts. Motion is small and functional: state changes ease over 160ms, the result headline "settles" (a 260ms blur-to-sharp) whenever the inputs change, and the mobile dock slides up once the result card has scrolled away.

Light is the default. Dark is a faithful mirror of the same world (deep navy ground, dimmed washes, translucent navy glass), selected by `prefers-color-scheme` or `[data-theme='dark']`. The direction refused a dark, heavy fintech dashboard; dark mode exists for comfort, not as the identity. Per PRODUCT.md, the surface must never borrow official or government cues (no Foru, Hacienda, or coat-of-arms imagery).
keyCharacteristics: Pale cool ground with three blurred colour washes behind everything.
Solid white cards for input; glass only where content moves underneath.
Exactly one gradient: the result card.
Onest variable, self-hosted, tabular figures everywhere.
Selected state is "raised": a white chip lifted out of a sunken track.
Lucide line icons at 16px, always paired with text.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The blue-violet-rose gradient appears once, on the result card. No buttons, headers, or badges borrow it.

rules.name: The Two Blues Rule
rules.body: `accent` marks and focuses; `button-fill` fills. Never put a white label on the dark-mode accent.

rules.name: The Receipt Figures Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on body and inherited everywhere. Amounts are never set in proportional figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase or letterspaced label styles; the only all-caps text is the two-letter language codes.

rules.name: The Glass Where It Moves Rule
rules.body: `backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(160-170%)` is reserved for surfaces content scrolls beneath: the header pill, the pinned result panel, and the mobile dock. Input cards stay solid.

rules.name: The Lit Edge Rule
rules.body: Every glass surface carries the inset top highlight and a `glass-line` border.

dos: Do keep input surfaces solid white (`surface`) with the Rest shadow and a 1px hairline.
Do reserve backdrop-filter glass, with the lit inner top edge, for surfaces content scrolls beneath.
Do keep tabular figures on every amount.
Do show choice as a raised white option in a sunken track (Raised chip shadow).
Do use `accent-ink` for blue text and `button-fill` for filled buttons, in both themes.
Do step corner radii down as surfaces nest (22 / 18 / 14 / 12 / 10px).
donts: Don't add a second gradient; the blue-violet-rose gradient belongs to the result card.
Don't make input cards translucent or blurred.
Don't turn the light working tool into a dark, heavy dashboard; dark mode mirrors the light world.
Don't use Foru, Hacienda, coat-of-arms, or other official-service cues.
Don't add uppercase, letterspaced labels above headings; headings and labels stay in sentence case.
Don't set amounts in proportional figures.
